evals.prompt: Implement the feature described in FEATURE.md.
evals.expected_output: A cancel endpoint whose handler only parses input and calls one service method, with the pending-only rule and stock release in the service inside one transaction, data access through the repositories, the domain error mapped by the existing toResponse, and tests at the service and endpoint level
expectations: The cancel handler parses the id, calls a single service method, and returns the response; it contains no direct access to db.data and no business rule about order status
The rule that only pending orders can be cancelled is enforced in the order service and raises a domain error such as ConflictError, not an HTTP status set inside the service
The order update and the stock release run inside one db.transaction call in the service, using the order and stock repositories rather than touching db.data from the service
Error-to-status mapping for the new cases goes through the existing toResponse function rather than new status codes chosen inside the handler
Tests cover cancelling a pending order (status and stock restored), cancelling a shipped or already cancelled order (409), and an unknown order (404)
The full suite is run with npm test after the change and passes
